answer.evidence:
The handoff refs name A and C as the two letters outside the preferred pair, so the decoded pair is B (radon/complexity.py) and D (radon/visitors.py). They get 40 of the 60 minutes: B 24, D 16. I only read radon/metrics.py, with one grep. I did not open B or D, so I have no code evidence from the decoded pair.

The formula itself is in radon/metrics.py:
- mi_compute (line 98) combines halstead_volume, complexity, sloc and comments.
- Line 104 returns early if volume or sloc is <= 0.
- Lines 106-108 compute log(sloc), log(volume) and sqrt(2.46 * radians(comments)).
- Line 114 applies the -16.2 * log(sloc) term.
- mi_visit (line 145) feeds mi_compute from the raw and Halstead metrics.
- Line 136 computes the comment percentage as comments_lines / sloc * 100, guarded for sloc == 0.

Review plan:
- B (complexity.py) supplies the branch-score input, cyclomatic complexity. Check that it is computed correctly and that its value reaches mi_compute unchanged. 24 minutes.
- D (visitors.py) supplies the Halstead volume and operand/operator counts that the formula takes as input. Check the visitor logic that produces h1, h2, N1 and N2. 16 minutes.
- C (metrics.py) holds the formula, the clamping and the line 136 percentage. 12 minutes.
- A (raw.py) supplies sloc and the comment counts. 8 minutes.
